p0_fix_proposals.p0: schemac_sql_postgres under linux-asan: Unix-socket path longer than 107 bytes
p0_fix_proposals.root_cause: WORK_DIR is ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/sql_postgres (tools/schemac/CMakeLists.txt:145). On Unix hosts, tools/schemac/tests/sql_postgres.cmake:58-61 puts the server's socket in that directory (pg_host = WORK_DIR; server option `-k ${WORK_DIR}`). The socket is then used by psql at :72, by pg_dump at :100 and when the server starts at :118-124. Linux sun_path holds 107 bytes plus a NUL. CI's build/linux-debug-asan tree gives "/home/runner/work/HeliosEngine/HeliosEngine/build/linux-debug-asan/tools/schemac/sql_postgres/.s.PGSQL.55439", which is 108 bytes, so PostgreSQL refuses the socket and pg_ctl start fails at :121-124. build/linux-gcc gives 101 bytes and passes. Nothing here is ASan-specific: any deeper build tree fails the same way (for example the agents' /home/user/wt/<task>/build/<task>-gcc trees).
p0_fix_proposals.proposed_fix:
Keep the data directory in WORK_DIR and move only the socket to a short private directory on Unix hosts (Windows keeps TCP).
1. In the non-Win32 branch at sql_postgres.cmake:58-61, run `execute_process(COMMAND mktemp -d /tmp/hpg.XXXXXX OUTPUT_VARIABLE sock_dir OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE RESULT_VARIABLE rc)`. mktemp creates the directory 0700.
2. When run_as is set, `chown nobody` the directory, as :49-51 already does for WORK_DIR.
3. Set `pg_host "${sock_dir}"` and `-k ${sock_dir}`.
4. Check `string(LENGTH "${sock_dir}/.s.PGSQL.${port}" n)` and fail with a clear FATAL_ERROR if it is over 107.
5. `file(REMOVE_RECURSE "${sock_dir}")` after `pg_ctl stop` (:202) and before each later FATAL_ERROR (:116, :123, :205).
The directory is unique per run, so parallel build trees stay isolated: the port is shared, but listen_addresses is empty, so only the socket path matters. To keep it from coming back, register a second schemac_sql_postgres variant whose -DWORK_DIR is deliberately longer than 110 bytes. The test, its checks and its timeout are unchanged.

p0_fix_proposals.p0: assetpipe_tests_perf: saveMeta p95 (and tonight moveAsset p95) above 50 ms on the hosted runner
p0_fix_proposals.root_cause:
Origin of the 50 ms budget: the plan does not set it. The module's own documents state it (engine/assetpipe/README.md:239-243, engine/assetpipe/tests/test_perf.cpp:11-13) as half of the smallest hot-reload build-step budget in docs/plan/02-engine-runtime.md §6.4 (Luau <= 100 ms p95 DEV, line 1818). Under 09 §5.8 it stays.

What each call does:
- saveMeta (engine/assetpipe/src/meta.cpp:761-797) lists directory 'a' once through DirectoryNames (meta.cpp:475-506). fs::listDirectory stats every entry for its size (engine/core/src/fs.cpp:216); at 2,000 entries that took 5.8–5.9 ms p50 on these runners.
- It then calls writeSidecar (meta.cpp:524-537): create a temp file, write it, fsync it (engine/core/src/platform/posix/posix_fs.cpp:86), rename it, and fsync the directory (posix_fs.cpp:90-103).
- moveAsset (meta.cpp:852-899) lists the directory and does two durable renames, so two directory fsyncs.

Why the tail is IO stalls: the deterministic part is under 10 ms. ensureMeta does the same listing and the same writeSidecar and measured p95 10.4 ms tonight and 7.2 ms on 10-05. Yet saveMeta p95 was 85.3 ms tonight and 101.7 ms on 10-05, and moveAsset 68.4 and 45.5 ms. The same binary passed in the ctest pass minutes earlier. So at least 4 of the 64 timed calls stalled for more than 50 ms, most plausibly in fsync or journal commits on the hosted runner's /tmp, which sits on the network-attached OS disk.

Why the test amplifies it: the timed loop (test_perf.cpp:193-203) alternates saveMeta with moveAsset's two directory fsyncs, and the p95 of 64 samples is the 4th-worst call. One commit stall spanning a few calls is therefore enough to fail the gate.

I did not build or strace this locally (the task said not to build).
p0_fix_proposals.proposed_fix:
These changes keep the 50,000 us CHECKs and the 2,000-entry setup.
1. moveAsset: rename the asset with fs::renameNoSync and make only the sidecar rename durable. Both targets are in parentOf(to), so one directory fsync persists both entries. That halves its fsyncs with the same durability on return (meta.cpp:539-551, :889-890).
2. DirectoryNames needs names only. Add a names-only option to core fs::ListOptions that skips entry.file_size (fs.cpp:216) and use it in DirectoryNames::names (meta.cpp:496). That removes 2,000 stats (about 5 ms) from every sidecar call.
3. Test method (test_perf.cpp:171-224):
   - Make the setup's 1,000 source writes durable before timing, so their writeback is not charged to timed calls.
   - Time saveMeta and moveAsset in separate loops.
   - Take p95 over 256 calls instead of 64, so a single stall is not the 95th percentile.
4. Before claiming the fix, confirm on the hosted runner which syscall carries the tail, for example with a per-phase breakdown in the MESSAGE or strace -T in a dispatched nightly.
p0_fix_proposals.files: engine/assetpipe/src/meta.cpp (:475-506, :524-551, :852-899); engine/core/include/helios/core/fs.h and engine/core/src/fs.cpp (:198-236, names-only listing); engine/assetpipe/tests/test_perf.cpp (:171-224)

p0_fix_proposals.p0: TestPerfDeepPaths on Windows Go (deep-paths read at most 2x the 4-level read)
p0_fix_proposals.root_cause:
What it measures (services/pkg/manifest/perf_test.go:109-141): wall-clock bestOf(3) (:36-43) of manifest.Parse, which covers zstd decode, BLAKE2b, decode and validate including the path-collision check. Two inputs of 64 MiB of 1,024-byte paths are compared: 508 levels deep, and 4 levels of 255-byte names. They are timed sequentially in the order deep, flat, vector, shuffled (:127-130), and the test fails if deep > 2*flat (:139).

The intrinsic ratio on hosted Windows is about 1.3–1.6x: tonight 382/293 ms = 1.30x, and attempt 1's vector read of identical deep content gave 374/237 = 1.58x. Attempt 1's synthetic deep read took 485 ms, 30 % slower than that identical-content vector read in the same process, giving 2.05x.

So the measurement is noisy at roughly ±30 %, against a margin of only about 25–50 %. Noise sources:
- `go test ./...` runs packages concurrently on the 4-vCPU runner (orchestrator about 70 s, hxl about 35 s). The deep and flat timing windows are seconds apart, so they see different load.
- Deep is timed first, so it absorbs heap growth (first-touch commit of about 100+ MB, costly on Windows) and the GC cycles triggered by building and marshalling the 64 MiB manifests.
- bestOf(3) in non-interleaved windows does not cancel a load shift between them.
p0_fix_proposals.proposed_fix:
Keep the 2x bound and both budgets; make the estimator robust.
1. Build all four inputs first and do one untimed warm-up Parse of each.
2. Run N = 7 interleaved rounds, timing deep, flat, vector and shuffled in each round. Call runtime.GC() before each timed Parse so collection of earlier garbage is not on the clock.
3. Keep the minimum per kind (the same estimator as bestOf) and check deep <= 2*flat, and the budgets, on those minima.
4. Print the ratio with %.2f. Today 2.05 prints as "2.0x" next to "(at most 2x)", which reads like a pass.
5. Log the ratio on passing runs too: run pkg/manifest's timing tests with -v or -json in ci.yml:232 so the next pass records its figure.
Cost: about 5 s more test time. No threshold moves and no skip.
p0_fix_proposals.files: services/pkg/manifest/perf_test.go (:36-43, :109-141); optionally .github/workflows/ci.yml:232 (verbose or json output for the record)

p0_fix_proposals.p0: editorui_ed15 timeout under linux-asan (2026-10-04 and again 2026-10-06)
p0_fix_proposals.root_cause:
The test (TIMEOUT 600, apps/tools/helios-uitest/CMakeLists.txt:48) runs in the clang Debug + ASan/UBSan build (CMakePresets linux-debug-asan: Debug, HELIOS_SANITIZE ON) on lavapipe. Suite::compareGolden (apps/tools/helios-uitest/main.cpp:216-248) skips FLIP only when a capture is bit-identical (:234-237). Otherwise it runs render::computeFlip on the whole image, which the code's own comment says costs 'about a minute per 1080p image in Debug sanitizer builds' (:233).

Tonight four captures (shell and grid at dark 100 % and 200 %) each differed by only 10–15 pixels and went through the full FLIP. hc 100 % was identical. The test was killed at 600.11 s right after 'viewport masked in shell_hc_200.png', inside that image's FLIP; 200 % captures have about 4x the pixels of 100 %. On 10-05 it passed in 320.83 s. So the runtime depends on how many captures happen to be bit-identical, and with several full-image FLIPs at -O0 with ASan it crosses 600 s.
p0_fix_proposals.proposed_fix:
Make FLIP's cost proportional to the difference while giving an identical result. FLIP's error at a pixel depends only on both images within the filter support (flipdetail::csfRadius(ppd) and featureRadius(ppd), engine/render/src/flip.cpp:164 and :226). A pixel whose support window contains no differing pixel therefore has error exactly 0.
1. Add render::computeFlipSparse, or do this in compareGolden:
   - Split the image into 64x64 tiles and keep the tiles whose window, dilated by R = csfRadius + featureRadius, contains a differing pixel.
   - Run the FLIP pipeline on each kept tile padded by R, clamped at the image borders exactly as the full-image filter clamps.
   - Accumulate in row-major order: the sum for mean over all W*H pixels, max, and countAbove.
2. Add a render_tests case asserting that the sparse result equals the full computeFlip (mean, max, countAbove) on random sparse diffs, including diffs at the image borders.
3. Optionally, also compile engine/render/src/flip.cpp and the PNG decode with -O2 in sanitizer builds (set_source_files_properties COMPILE_OPTIONS); they stay instrumented.
TIMEOUT 600, the FLIP limits (mean 0.01, hot 0.1 %) and the captures are unchanged.
p0_fix_proposals.files: apps/tools/helios-uitest/main.cpp (:216-248); engine/render/src/flip.cpp and engine/render/include/helios/render/flip.h (sparse or tiled evaluation); engine/render/tests (equality test); optionally engine/render/CMakeLists.txt (per-source -O2 under HELIOS_SANITIZE)

p0_fix_proposals.p0: NEW: NS-0.7 trunk drops on hosted Windows after WP-0.13r (RIO)
p0_fix_proposals.root_cause:
This is likely a capacity regression from WP-0.13r's Registered I/O path (#62).

Evidence it is tied to RIO:
- Hosted Windows NS-0.7 passed with 0 % drops at 20,000 pps on 10-04 and 10-05 on WSASendMsg/WSARecvMsg (rcvbuf 32768 KB).
- Tonight, on RIO, it dropped 1.5222 %. rcvbuf 31774 KB means 15,887 slots of 2 KB.

Why RIO has less buffer: according to engine/net/src/platform/win32/win32_udp_socket.cpp:175-184, a RIO socket keeps no buffer of its own. A datagram that arrives while every receive slot is completed but not yet re-posted is dropped.
- Receive side: slotsFor() counts a 2,112-byte stride per datagram (:192-196, :426), so the trunk buffers 15,887 datagrams, about 0.79 s at 20k pps. The 32 MB AFD buffer held roughly 26–27k datagrams of 1.2 KB.
- Send side: capped at 2,048 slots (:190, :427). postSend returns Full when no slot frees after one flush and reap (:477-481), and sendTo and sendBatch count that as sendWouldBlock and drop the datagram (:693, :749).

Why it showed tonight: the hosted VM was loaded (NS-0.2 cross-checks showed +26 % and +35 % CPU outside the thread, and 0.78–0.84 background cores). Stalls that the old buffers absorbed now overflow. The same build passed with 0 % drops on the quiet 12-thread win-gpu box.

What is not known: the NS-0.7 line (net_bench.cpp:233-240) prints no sendWouldBlock or receive counters, so which side dropped cannot be told from the log. There is a single occurrence so far.
p0_fix_proposals.proposed_fix:
No change to NS-0.7's thresholds.
1. Attribute the drops first. Add both sockets' UdpSocketStats (sendWouldBlock, sendErrors, receiveErrors, truncated) and cellEvents.lost to TrunkGateResult and to the NS-0.7 report line (engine/net/bench/trunk_gate.h, net_bench.cpp:233-240). Add a RIO counter for 'all receive slots completed and not re-posted' in receiveBatch (win32_udp_socket.cpp:820-873).
2. Restore buffer parity with the plain socket:
   - Size receive slots from the largest datagram the endpoint sends instead of 2 KB, for example 1,280 + 64 bytes for netcode's 1.2 KB packets.
   - Raise kMaxReceiveSlots so a 32 MB SO_RCVBUF request yields at least as many datagrams as AFD held (about 25k; locked memory stays about 34 MB per trunk socket).
   - Let send slots follow SO_SNDBUF for trunk sockets instead of capping at 2,048.
   - On Full, reap in a short bounded loop before dropping; loopback sends complete within microseconds.
3. Add a Windows net_tests case that stalls the receiver for about 1 s at 20k pps with 32 MB buffers and asserts zero loss on both the RIO and the WSARecvMsg paths.
